title: Veterans Pension — Counting Retroactive Compensation Releases by Date of Deposit
content:
# Deposit date of retroactive Disability Compensation releases — Veterans Pension statement

A retroactive Disability Compensation release is one-time income that counts for the twelve months after it was deposited. In the veteran's benefit income statement on his Veterans Pension award, the releases therefore count by when the most recent of them was deposited — the payment date of the latest retroactive release in the Disability Compensation payment ledger — measured in days to the date of the statement — the date the statement carries, the day the change began, and not the day the veteran files it:

| Most recent release deposited | The releases count |
|---|---|
| within the fresh period: 90 days or fewer before the statement | in full |
| more than 90 days but no more than 365 days (one year) before the statement | for the months left of its twelve-month year divided by 12 — that is, 12 less the whole months from the deposit to the date of the statement, divided by 12 |
| more than 365 days before the statement | not at all |

The weight is applied to the releases less any representative's fee taken out of them, and the result is rounded to the cent.

## Basis Q&A (hypothetical deposits)

*Deposited 90 days before the statement?* Within the fresh period: in full.

*Deposited 100 days before, which is 3 whole months before?* After the fresh period and within one year: 12 less 3 is 9 months left, so 9 divided by 12 of the releases counts. On releases of 6000.00 that is 4500.00.

*Deposited 300 days before, 9 whole months before?* 3 months left: 3 divided by 12 counts.

*Deposited 365 days before?* Still within one year, so the months-left weight governs. At 366 days or more nothing counts.

*Statement dated 2025-11-30, filed 2026-03-10, release deposited 2025-08-12?* The count runs from 2025-08-12 to 2025-11-30: 110 days, 3 whole months, so 9 divided by 12 counts. The filing day does not enter the count.
